   232	emit unchecked declarations. The authoritative supervisor build therefore
   233	runs with `Tablet/` read-only and independently replays every built Tablet
   234	module through `leanchecker` before recording artifact provenance or making
   235	the artifact reusable. A replay failure rejects and purges the whole requested
   236	Tablet closure; syntax bans remain defense in depth.
   237	
   238	The marker line may be at any indentation (`--` line comments are indentation-inert in Lean). Do not put the literal text `-- BODY` (whitespace-trimmed, on its own line) inside any `/-…-/` block comment in a tablet file — the splitter does not distinguish the two.
   239	
   240	Existing deterministic checks also enforce related Lean hygiene:
   241	
   242	- unauthorized imports are rejected
   243	- node-marker mismatches are rejected
   244	- `sorry` inside definitions is rejected
   245	- declaration-name mismatches are rejected
   246	- **missing or duplicate `-- BODY` marker is rejected**
   247	- **missing or duplicate `-- [TABLET NODE: NodeName]` marker is rejected**
   248	- **an `import` line at or after the `-- [TABLET NODE: ...]` marker is rejected**
   249	- **the line immediately preceding `-- BODY` not ending with `:=`, `by`, or `where` is rejected**
   250	- **an anonymous `instance` (no name) is rejected**
   251	- **a bare-pipe `inductive` (not using the `where` form) is rejected**
   252	
   253	### Preamble import convention (auto-applied)
   254	
   255	Every tablet node should transitively `import Tablet.Preamble`, either
   256	directly or via another tablet node's import. This guarantees a single
   257	shared root for the import DAG and keeps shared dependencies consolidated
   258	in `Tablet/Preamble.lean`.
   259	
   260	**Auto-fix:** the supervisor runs an idempotent normalization sweep at
   261	worker-acceptance time. For every node `Tablet/<X>.lean` whose import set
   262	contains neither `import Tablet.Preamble` nor any other `import Tablet.<Y>`,
   263	the supervisor inserts `import Tablet.Preamble` at the top of the imports
   264	block. This means workers do not need to remember the convention — a node
   265	that ships with only Mathlib imports will be rewritten in place to also
   266	import the preamble before validation runs.
   267	
   268	Best practice: put shared imports and any cross-cutting open declarations
   269	in `Tablet/Preamble.lean` so every node picks them up via the transitive
   270	import. Node-local imports (those that only one node needs) can stay in
   271	the node file.
   272	
   273	Implementation: `kernel/src/filespec.rs:ensure_preamble_import_for_orphan` +
   274	`normalize_node_lean_imports_on_disk`, invoked from
   275	`runtime_cli.rs:check_trellis_worker_result_output` over
   276	`current_present_nodes` on every accept.
   277	
   278	## Lean source layout under `Tablet/`
   279	
   280	All Lean source under `Tablet/` must live in either `Tablet/Preamble.lean`
   281	or `Tablet/<NodeName>.lean` for some registered tablet node. Subdirectories
   282	are not allowed (no `Tablet/Support/X.lean`), and a top-level
   283	`Tablet/<X>.lean` whose stem `X` is not a registered node is also not
   284	allowed. Shared declarations belong in `Tablet/Preamble.lean`; anything
   285	larger should be factored into a real registered tablet node. This is
   286	enforced at worker-acceptance time: any offending `.lean` file under
   287	`Tablet/` produces a per-path rejection naming the file.
   288	
   289	## Practical guidance
   290	
   291	- Do not put free exposition, section headers, or manuscript-style narrative at top level in a node `.tex` file.
   292	- If a node really contains two separate mathematical claims, split it into two nodes instead of placing multiple top-level statement blocks in one `.tex` file.
   293	- If background notation or macros are needed globally, add them to `Tablet/header.tex`, not `Preamble.tex`.
   294	- If the file shape you want does not fit this spec, that is usually a sign the DAG needs restructuring rather than a sign that the spec should be ignored.
   295	
   296	## Protected correspondence (paper-target preservation)
   297	
   298	After a human expert approves a paper target at the advance-gate, the kernel
   299	snapshots the set of **covering nodes** (the tablet nodes whose statements
   300	the target claims) and baselines their "correspondence fingerprint." From
   301	that point on, any subsequent worker commit that would cause a covering
   302	node's correspondence to "reopen" is rejected at commit time (outside
   303	`coarse_restructure` mode).
   304	
   305	### What the correspondence fingerprint captures
   306	
   307	For a given node, its correspondence fingerprint is a hash of:
   308	
   309	1. The node's own `.tex` statement block.
   310	2. The Lean-semantic closure of the node's Lean declaration — the
   311	   transitive serialization of every `const` it references (theorem types,
   312	   definition values, inductive/constructor shapes, axiom types, ...).
   313	   **Proof bodies are NOT in this closure.** Changing a proof body of a
   314	   dependency does not change this hash; changing the declared type of a
   315	   referenced theorem, or the value of a referenced definition, DOES.
   316	3. The `.tex` statements of every `definition`-kind descendant in the
   317	   node's Lean-import closure (via `import Tablet.X` lines). Only
   318	   descendants that were already present at the moment the current
   319	   baseline was captured count. A worker adding a new definition helper
   320	   post-baseline does not by itself trigger a reopen; the new helper
   321	   enters the baseline at the next correspondence verification.
   322	4. The preamble's structured `.tex` content.
   323	
   324	### What "reopen" means
   325	
   326	A covering node's correspondence is "reopened" by a commit if the
   327	prospective post-commit fingerprint differs from the approval baseline
   328	along any of these axes:
   329	
   330	- Own `.tex` statement changed.
   331	- Lean-semantic closure changed (something referenced by the node's Lean
   332	  declaration no longer has the same meaning).
   333	- A baselined definition-descendant's `.tex` statement changed, or the
   334	  descendant is no longer reachable from the node's Lean-import closure.
   335	- The preamble's `.tex` structured content changed.
   336	
   337	If any of those happen on a covering node, the commit is rejected and the
   338	agent receives a prose error enumerating which axis differed.
   339	
   340	### What is allowed (not a reopen)
   341	
   342	- Proof-body changes — your own or dependencies'.
   343	- Adding new helper nodes (proof-kind or definition-kind) below the
   344	  covering node.
   345	- Renaming local identifiers inside proofs.
   346	- Any change on a non-covering node, as long as it does not cascade into
   347	  a meaning-change of the covering node's Lean-semantic closure.
   348	
   349	In general: you may freely modify the proof machinery, but you must
   350	preserve the covering node's declared mathematical content and the
   351	definitions it was baselined against.
   352	
   353	### The `coarse_restructure` escape hatch
   354	
   355	Genuine expert-approved changes to a covering node's statement or its
   356	supporting definition package require `coarse_restructure` mode. Requests
   357	for that mode must come from a reviewer — workers cannot enter
   358	`coarse_restructure` on their own. The mode bypasses the reopen guard
   359	entirely, on the assumption that the human-in-the-loop review step
   360	re-approves the modified target.
   361	
   362	### What workers see in each request
   363	
   364	The worker request carries:
   365	
   366	- `approved_target_nodes`: the covering-node set snapshotted at the last
   367	  advance-gate approval.
   368	- `approved_corr_fingerprints`: the JSON-encoded
   369	  `CorrespondenceFingerprint` baseline for each covering node.
   370	
   371	These are the exact nodes / fingerprints the commit-time guard will
   372	compare against. Workers can precompute whether their planned delta
   373	would trip the guard by reasoning about whether it affects any of the
   374	four axes above on any `approved_target_nodes` entry.

     3	$x\in\mathsf{IncSeq}$ whose range is exactly $X$.
     4	\end{lemma}
     5	\begin{proof}
     6	We construct a map $x:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ by least-element recursion.  First,
     7	$X$ is nonempty, since an empty set is finite, so let $x(0)$ be the least
     8	element of $X$.  Suppose that $x(k)\in X$ has already been defined.  The set
     9	
    10	\[
    11	X_{>x(k)}=\{m\in X\mid x(k)<m\}
    12	\]
    13	
    14	is nonempty.  Indeed, if it were empty, then every element of $X$ would be
    15	at most $x(k)$, so $X\subseteq\{0,1,\ldots,x(k)\}$.  The latter is finite,
    16	and hence $X$ would be finite, contradicting the hypothesis.  Therefore the
    17	well-ordering of $\mathbb N$ gives a least element of $X_{>x(k)}$; define
    18	$x(k+1)$ to be that element.  This also proves inductively that
    19	
    20	\[
    21	x(k)\in X\quad\text{and}\quad x(k)<x(k+1)
    22	\]
    23	
    24	for every $k$.  If $i<j$, repeated use of these inequalities gives
    25	$x(i)<x(j)$.  Conversely, if $x(i)<x(j)$ and $j\leq i$, monotonicity gives
    26	$x(j)\leq x(i)$, a contradiction.  Thus $x$ preserves and reflects the
    27	order on $\mathbb N$.  By the definition of $\mathsf{IncSeq}$ in
    28	\noderef{IncSeq}, this makes $x$ an element of $\mathsf{IncSeq}$, and the
    29	induction just given shows $\operatorname{range}(x)\subseteq X$.
    30	
    31	It remains to prove the reverse inclusion.  For each fixed $n\in X$, put
    32	
    33	\[
    34	F_n=\{m\in X\mid m<n\}.
    35	\]
    36	
    37	This is finite because it is contained in the finite initial segment
    38	$\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$.  We prove simultaneously for every $j\in\mathbb N$
    39	that, whenever $n\in X$ and $|F_n|=j$, the recursion lists precisely the
    40	members of $F_n$ before reaching $n$: namely,
    41	
    42	\[
    43	x(j)=n
    44	\qquad\text{and}\qquad
    45	\{x(i)\mid i<j\}=F_n.
    46	\]
